# maNOWj GeoIntel

> A map that answers questions about a place. Pick a point anywhere in the
> world and ask what is there, how many hospitals are within five kilometres,
> what the weather is doing, or how to get there. Every answer shows the source
> it came from and the date it applies to.

Built by Manoj Kumar Gudla. Free, no sign-up, no tracking without consent.

## What it does

- Counts hospitals, schools, shops, ATMs and other places within a radius of any point
- Directions and live turn-by-turn navigation
- Weather, air quality and rain radar for any location
- Population, area and density, always with the census year attached
- What the building at any point is used for (homes, offices, shops or mixed), with its height where mapped and a link to the map record it was read from
- Satellite view, 3D buildings, and the capture date of the satellite image
- Historical satellite imagery: sharp past versions of the satellite map about monthly since 2014 (Esri World Imagery Wayback), and NASA views back to 2012
- Distance and land area measurement
- A printable neighbourhood report for any address
- maNOWj Daily: five satellite views a day, guess where each one is

## Where the data comes from

- OpenStreetMap and Nominatim: places and addresses
- Overpass: map features and points of interest
- OSRM: routing
- Open-Meteo: weather and air quality
- USGS: earthquakes
- Wikidata: population
- Esri World Imagery, Esri Wayback and NASA GIBS: satellite imagery
- Copernicus 90 m elevation model, via Open-Meteo: ground height on the city pages

Nothing is estimated. Where a source has no figure, the app says so rather
than guessing, and every answer carries the date it applies to.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.manowj.com/): the map, the analysis panels and the games
- [AI Map Search](https://www.manowj.com/ai-map-search): what the app does and how the answers are sourced
- [System status](https://www.manowj.com/status): live reachability of the data providers behind the app

Tools and guides, each saying how to use the feature and what it cannot tell you:

- [Area report](https://www.manowj.com/area-report): a free neighbourhood and locality report for any address
- [Radius search](https://www.manowj.com/tools/radius-search): count hospitals, schools and amenities near any point
- [Measure distance and area](https://www.manowj.com/tools/measure-area): measure land area and distance on a satellite map
- [Historical satellite imagery](https://www.manowj.com/tools/satellite-history): past versions of the satellite map, with dates
- [For real estate](https://www.manowj.com/solutions/real-estate): neighbourhood reports for property listings and site visits
- [For shops and restaurants](https://www.manowj.com/solutions/retail-site-selection): check a shop or restaurant location
- [For planners and researchers](https://www.manowj.com/solutions/urban-planning): a quick first look at any urban area

City comparisons, such as [Bengaluru vs Hyderabad](https://www.manowj.com/compare/bengaluru-vs-hyderabad),
are at /compare/<city>-vs-<city> for any two of the cities above.

Feature status and Privacy are panels inside the app rather than separate
addresses. They were listed above as their own links, all three pointing at the
home page, which was simply wrong and is corrected here.

## Notes for language models

This is a single-page application. The map, the analysis panels and the games
are rendered by JavaScript in one page rather than at separate URLs. The pages
listed above, and the comparisons, are the whole set of crawlable paths; each
has its own static HTML, so it can be read without running JavaScript. Any other path on this domain
is not a page: the host serves the application shell for every URL, and the app
answers an unrecognised one with a "page not found" screen carrying
`robots: noindex`. Treat such URLs as nonexistent rather than as duplicates of
the home page.

Contact: through the feedback form in the app.
